text:
Maria (Support): Heads up — AcmeOps reporting intermittent 429s starting ~09:12 UTC. Spike concentrated in the last 8-12s of each minute. Can SRE take a look? :eyes:

Kevin (SRE): Got it. Can you paste a sample trace id and the token type (long-lived vs ephemeral)? Also whether they're on HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.

Maria (Support): trace-284a1b2c. Token: long-lived API key reused across many Lambdas. They say ~500 concurrent workers at :00.

Jess (Infra): Likely minute-boundary refill stampede. Even with good per-second throughput, minute RPM windows can exhaust if traffic clusters. Do they fanout per job or batch requests?

Sam (Support): They fanout — each cron invocation spawns 5 parallel calls. Suggested quick repro they can run from a container:

`````
seq 1 500 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <THEIR_TOKEN>" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
`````

Kevin (SRE): Good. Ask them to paste a raw 429 response (headers + body). We surface x-rw-rpm-limit, x-rw-rpm-remaining, Retry-After — those prove window exhaustion.

Alex (Platform): Note: platform smoothing changed recently; multiplexed tokens + HTTP/2 can look burstier. A single connection with many streams can make the minute-slot usage spike.

Jess (Infra): Short-term mitigations: 1) jitter cron across [0,60s]; 2) implement client-side leaky-bucket to cap per-second concurrency; 3) upgrade SDK if on older client that reuses connections badly.

Sam (Support): Offered temporary quota bump while they implement fixes.

ratebot: quota adjustment applied (change_id: qadj-2840) — tenant acmeops RPM +2x for 15 minutes.

Maria (Support): Ops applied the bump and we're monitoring. I'll ask customer to run repro and send 429 headers. :thumbsup:

Kevin (SRE): Internally: watch for sustained >70% of new RPM for >5m. If persistent, propose reserved capacity or a dedicated pool.

Sam (Support): Noted SDK mention — v0.9.2 amplifies minute-boundary bursts; v0.9.4 has smoothing and concurrency controls. Flagging SDK eng.

Alex (Platform): Confirmed. Sent upgrade note.

Maria (Support): Customer will run repro, collect the headers, upgrade SDK, and add jitter. They'll report back in ~1h.

Kevin (SRE): If it reoccurs, capture a 60s pcap and correlate ingress timestamps with our RPM bucket allocation. Also capture x-rw-* headers to verify consumption.

Jess (Infra): Keep an eye on HTTP/2 stream counts — many streams hide concurrency from naive client metrics.

Maria (Support): Closing the escalation once we see reduction in 429s or identify a persistent trend. Thanks all.
